sections.heading: C — Licensing and occupant protection
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing and occupant protection

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
A person driving a motor vehicle on a New Mexico public road needs a driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
A New Mexico resident is also required to hold a New Mexico driver license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Applicants younger than eighteen use the graduated licensing system until they qualify for an unrestricted license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
The graduated system progresses through an instructional permit, a provisional license and an unrestricted license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
An instructional permit authorizes driving under the supervision of a licensed driver aged at least twenty-one who can operate that vehicle type. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
For a passenger car driven on an instructional permit, the supervising driver occupies the front passenger seat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Eligibility for an instructional permit begins at age fifteen. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
An instructional permit applicant must pass both the knowledge examination and the vision examination. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
An applicant younger than eighteen needs a parent or guardian to sign the consent form. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
The instructional permit must be held for a minimum of six months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
A person aged fifteen or older seeking the instructional permit must attend an approved driver education course that includes DWI instruction and driving practice. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
Instructional-permit driving may be supervised by an approved instructor seated beside the learner. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A01
The alternative supervising driver must be at least twenty-one and have held a license in this or another state for at least three years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A01
Without a licensed adult aged twenty-one or older in the vehicle, a provisional driver may carry at most one nonfamily passenger younger than twenty-one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A01
A provisional-license applicant needs at least fifty hours of practice behind the wheel. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A01
At least ten of the required practice hours for a provisional license must occur at night. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A01
The learner’s parent or guardian certifies completion of the required driving practice. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A01
To receive a provisional license, the applicant must pass written and road examinations as well as vision screening. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A01
The earliest provisional-license age is fifteen years and six months after holding an instructional permit for six months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
A provisional applicant must have no traffic-violation conviction in the preceding ninety days. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
An unrestricted-license applicant must have held a provisional license throughout the immediately preceding twelve months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
A person applying for an unrestricted license must have no traffic-violation conviction during the previous ninety days. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
An unrestricted-license applicant must have no pending traffic violations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A02
During the provisional period, an unrestricted-license applicant must have neither a guilty adjudication nor a pending offense involving alcohol or drugs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

Misconceptions: provisional permission differs from unrestricted permission; each level has its own conditions.
Mnemonics: permit, provisional, unrestricted names the progression described on the licensing pages.
Glossary: instructional permit means supervised permission; provisional license is the intermediate stage.
Dynamic facts: licensing conditions, restraint thresholds and agency contact details require current issuer confirmation before release.

sections.heading: C2 — Licensing and occupant protection
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Licensing and occupant protection

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A02
A provisional license normally bars public-highway driving from midnight until five in the morning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A02
The provisional nighttime restriction does not apply when a licensed driver aged twenty-one or older accompanies the driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A02
Family necessity is a permitted reason for provisional nighttime driving when supported by a parent’s or guardian’s signed statement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A02
Medical necessity permits provisional nighttime driving when a parent or guardian provides a signed statement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
Travel between home and work is an exception to the provisional nighttime restriction when the employer supplies a signed statement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
Travel to or from school or a religious activity is a provisional nighttime exception with a signed statement from a school official, religious official, parent or guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A02
A medical emergency is another exception to the provisional nighttime driving restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A02
The handbook describes driver licenses as having either four-year or eight-year validity. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A02
The renewal window described in the handbook begins ninety days before expiration and ends thirty days afterward. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A02
For renewal, the handbook directs a driver to bring the existing license and another identity document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A02
Renewal can require vision or knowledge testing and, in special cases, a driving examination. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A02
A conviction for driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs can result in loss of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A02
Refusing an alcohol or drug test requested by a police officer can cost a driver the privilege to drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A02
Leaving a crash without providing identification can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A02
False information on a driver-license application can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A02
An unpaid financial judgment for motor-vehicle-crash damages can put driving privileges at risk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A02
Altering license information or using another person’s license to try to buy alcohol can cost driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A02
Failing to attend a reexamination requested by MVD can jeopardize the driver license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A03
Using a vehicle for a felony or causing a death in a vehicle crash can result in loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A03
Accumulating excessive driving-record points can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A03
Allowing another person to use your driver license can lead to loss of driving privileges. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A03
Before driving, buckle your belt and check that every passenger uses a belt or a child restraint. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A03
The handbook directs drivers to lock the vehicle doors before setting off. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A03
Using a safety belt reduces the chance of death or injury in a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R25 | anchor: A03
The handbook states that driving without a safety belt violates New Mexico law. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R26 | anchor: A03
A two-part belt system provides its intended protection when both its lap portion and its shoulder portion are worn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R27 | anchor: A03
An automatic shoulder belt still requires fastening the separate lap belt. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R28 | anchor: A03
The staged handbook says children younger than twelve must use appropriate restraints whenever the vehicle moves. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R29 | anchor: A03
The staged handbook says a child younger than twenty-four months or lighter than sixty pounds must use an approved safety device. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R30 | anchor: A03
The handbook directs caregivers to secure children in the rear seat. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R31 | anchor: A03
The handbook warns against placing a child in the front passenger position, especially where an air bag could deploy. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R32 | anchor: A03
Organizations may lend a child safety device to a caregiver who cannot afford one. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R33 | anchor: A03
The handbook gives the Traffic Safety Bureau information numbers as 505-827-0427 and 1-800-541-7952. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0006]
